I wonder, can I use prepared statements (in transaction mode) as long as they are prepared and used in the same transaction?

so:

1. begin transaction
2. do some sql
3. prepare statement
4. use prepared statement a few time
5. release prepared statement
6. do some other sql stuff
7. commit

Will this at least work? 

**Update**: Added releasing prepared statement step

@CySlider until transaction is finished client is bound to server connection. There is no problem with this scenario.

Release 1.3 will also add support for protocol-level prepared statements. You will be able :
1. Parse statement X
2. Bind X to parameter values (execute). Commit.
3. Bind X to parameter values (execute) again. Commit.
4. Bind X to parameter values (execute) again. Commit.

So that prepared statement X will survive through transaction boundaries. But this only applies to protocol-level prepared statements. SQL-level PREPARE won't work after transaction is committed or rolled back.

Thanks!

by design, the auth_query function uses postgres user credentials on a target server to authenticate clients, so working auth_query must be:

and preparations for it
